fatal_errors: The proposed nickel- or titanium-based alloys do not reconstruct the target ZrB2 cermet containing 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder.
The response omits spark-plasma sintering and the critical 1500 °C processing optimum.
Protective oxidation in air is not evidence of resistance to dissolution and reaction in molten aluminum; the proposed oxide-layer mechanism is unsupported for the stated environment.
The cited studies concern general high-temperature or oxidation behavior of refractory high-entropy alloys, not nickel- or titanium-based components immersed in molten aluminum.
No evidence supports the claimed material choices under the relevant 700 °C, multiday molten-aluminum exposure.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad engineering problem—high-temperature molten-aluminum attack on dipping equipment—and proposes a comparative corrosion/service-life test. However, it misses the target material, composition, SPS processing study, 1500 °C densification optimum, pore-filling mechanism, and measured corrosion, wear, hardness, and toughness outcomes. Its evidence only establishes generic high-temperature or oxidation properties and cannot validate nickel- or titanium-based alloys in molten aluminum. Because the central intervention and mechanism are both unsupported, this is not a defensible alternative to the target.
